```{r}
#| label = "setup",
#| eval = FALSE
library(rpkgkit)
dir <- tempdir()
dir.create(dir)
usethis::create_package(dir)

```

# Import standalone helpers

`rpkgkit` includes utilities that can also be imported directly into another
project with `usethis::use_standalone()`.

```r
usethis::use_standalone("WangLabCSU/rpkgkit", "args_to_func")
```

## Match arguments to functions

The `args_to_func.R` standalone script provides helpers for matching a list of
arguments to compatible functions.

```{r}
#| label = "match_func_to_args",
#| eval = FALSE
f1 <- function(a, b) a + b
f2 <- function(x, y, ...) x * y
f3 <- function(p, q) p - q

args <- list(a = 1, b = 2)
match_func_to_args(args, f1, f2, f3)
```

```{r}
#| label = "filter_args_for_func",
#| eval = FALSE
args <- list(a = 1, b = 2, x = 3, y = 4)
foo <- function(x, y = 1) x + y
filter_args_for_func(args, foo)
```

## Show the caller of a cli message

The `caller_cli.R` standalone script decorates a `cli` function so its output
identifies the caller.

```{r}
#| label = "caller_cli",
#| eval = FALSE
decorated <- add_caller_to_cli(cli::cli_alert_info)
foo1 <- \() {
  decorated("<- where is this called from?")
}
foo2 <- \() foo1()
bar <- function() foo2()
bar()
```

## Use colored cli output

The `colorful_cli.R` standalone script creates a `cli` environment with
convenient color classes.

```{r}
#| label = "colorful_cli",
#| eval = FALSE
color_cli <- create_colorful_cli_env()
color_cli$cli_alert_danger("{.red This is a red message}")
color_cli$cli_alert_info("{.blue This is a blue message}")
color_cli$cli_alert_info("{.orange This is an orange message}")

color_cli2 <- create_colorful_cli_env(cli_theme = generate_color_theme())
color_cli2$cli_alert_success(
  "{.violetred3 R}{.orange a}{.yellow i}{.green n}{.cyan b}{.blue o}{.purple w}"
)
```

## Add timestamps to cli output

The `ts_cli.R` standalone script creates timestamped `cli` functions.

```{r}
#| label = "ts_cli",
#| eval = FALSE
ts_cli <- create_ts_cli_env()
ts_cli$cli_alert_info("Hello, world!")
```

## Print frequency tables

The `cli_table.R` standalone script prints frequency tables of a vector with
cli styling. `cli_table()` uses two aligned lines (headers, then counts), while
`cli_table_oneline()` collapses them into a single `header: count` line. Both
return the underlying `table` object invisibly.

```{r}
#| label = "cli_table",
#| eval = FALSE
x <- c("apple", "pear", "apple", NA)

cli_table(x)
cli_table(x, head_format = ".strong", align = "center")

cli_table_oneline(x)
cli_table_oneline(mtcars$cyl, sep = " | ", count_format = NULL)
```

## Validate and transform arguments

The `make_arg_validator.R` standalone script builds reusable validators. Give
it an unquoted block of checks and coercions written in terms of argument
names; it returns a function that, called from inside your function, returns
the validated arguments as a named list.

```{r}
#| label = "make_arg_validator",
#| eval = FALSE
validate_add <- make_arg_validator({
  if (!type %in% c("sum", "product")) {
    rlang::abort("`type` must be \"sum\" or \"product\".", call = NULL)
  }
  n <- as.integer(max(n, 1L))
})

add <- function(type = c("sum", "product"), n = 1L) {
  args <- validate_add()
  switch(args$type, sum = sum(1:args$n), product = prod(1:args$n))
}

add("sum", 3)
```

Errors raised inside the block reach the caller unchanged, and an assignment
to an existing argument is written back through the returned list:

```{r}
#| label = "validate_add",
#| eval = FALSE
try(list2env(validate_add(), envir = environment()))
```

Only names that already existed in the caller's frame are returned, so a
validator updates arguments but never adds new ones. The same validator can be
shared by several functions, and `env` can be passed explicitly to validate a
list of options instead of a function frame.

# Manage standalone files in a package

Use `inquire_standalone()` to inspect standalone files in a GitHub repository
and `browse_standalone()` to search supported repositories.

```{r}
#| label = "inquire"
try(inquire_standalone("r-lib/rlang")) |> head()
```

```{r}
#| label = "browse"
try(browse_standalone()) |> head()
```

Create a local standalone file with a standard metadata header:

```{r}
#| label = "create"
dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "R")
create_standalone("foo", path = dir, open = FALSE)
```

## Validate the standalone file layout

`check_standalone()` verifies that a custom standalone file follows the layout
consumed by `usethis::use_standalone()`. It checks the `# ---` header (the
required `repo`, `file`, `last-updated` and `license` slots, the optional
`imports` slot, and the format of each value), that every documented function
carries `@noRd`, and that a `# nocov start` marker precedes all functions.

```{r}
#| label = "check_standalone"
check_standalone(path = file.path(dir, "standalone-foo.R"))
```

Findings are printed in the style of `devtools::check()`, and the counts are
returned invisibly as `list(error = , warning = , note = )`. An error in a check
point skips the remaining ones, while warnings and notes never stop the run.

After editing standalone files, refresh their `last-updated` field:

```{r}
#| label = "update timestamp"
update_time_in_standalone(path = file.path(dir, "standalone-foo.R"))
```

Add a dated changelog entry to one or more standalone files:

```{r}
#| label = "add changelog",
#| eval = FALSE
add_changelog_in_standalone(
  path = file.path(dir, "standalone-foo.R"),
  "Added foo function"
)
```
